item.title: Two Spurs stars return to training ahead of Ipswich clash
item.description: Two Spurs stars return to training ahead of Ipswich clash Savio and Lucas Bergvall were both back in Tottenham training ahead of their match against Ipswich this weekend. item.title: Max Verstappen: “I really thought that we would not win a race this year”
item.description: Motorsport photo Heading into the Las Vegas Grand Prix on a run of eight consecutive podiums, Max Verstappen looks every bit the force who dominated Formula 1 earlier this decade. Back in March, however, the four-time world champion was braced for his first winless campaign since 2015. Speaking during Las Vegas media day, Verstappen reflected on the scale of Red Bull Racing ’s mid-season recovery during Formula 1’s sweeping 2026 chassis and engine overhaul - the team’s first year running its in-house Red Bull Ford power unit. "Did I personally expect it to be like this after the first few rounds? For sure not," Verstappen said. "I really thought that we would not win a race this year and now we are constantly fighting for a win or close to it." Read Also: Fan voting opens for the Autosport Awards Across the first three rounds in Australia, China, and Japan, Verstappen managed just 12 points - finishing sixth in Melbourne, retiring in Shanghai, and crossing eighth at Suzuka - while publicly describing the RB22 as "completely undriveable" in China due to acute cornering balance issues. He went four races without a podium and endured 15 grands prix without P1, absorbing four retirements across China, Monaco, Great Britain, and the Netherlands. Fixing the car and learning the engine Asked whether Red Bull’s 2026 recovery mirrored its adjustments from a year earlier, Verstappen shut down the comparison immediately. "No, no, not related at all. Because we, this year, have very, very different problems to last year," he said. "So, it was a combination of putting more performance on the car, but at the same time also just fixing some of our problems, which automatically would give us more performance." That step-by-step progress extended beyond aerodynamics. "Also, engine side, we understood a lot more what we wanted from the engine," Verstappen noted. "Still, there’s always room for improvement; we know that. That’s what we are constantly working on." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing The payoff arrived in autumn. Verstappen broke his P1 drought on 4 October in Malaysia, swept the sprint and grand prix in Singapore a week later, and added a third victory in Mexico City on 1 November. Coupled with second place in São Paulo, the surge lifted him to second in the drivers’ championship on 279 points - 111 behind newly crowned champion Kimi Antonelli, yet 17 clear of George Russell - while keeping Red Bull third in the constructors’ fight. "Hats off to the whole team; they’ve done a really good job," Verstappen said. "But now, we also look forward, and yeah, still look into some of the weaknesses that we have and things that we want to change for next year to hopefully make the car even better." item.title: Tonda Eckert signs Southampton contract extension after ‘Spygate’ scandal
item.description: Tonda Eckert has signed a contract extension at Southampton after surviving the storm of the ‘Spygate’ scandal. Eckert found himself under immense scrutiny after Southampton were caught spying on their Championship play-off semi-final opponents Middlesbrough last season. An investigation found Saints had also spied on two other teams that seasons and the club were subsequently kicked out of the Championship play-off final and docked four points at the start of the season season, admitting to three breaches of EFL regulations. Eckert accepted responsibility and was given a six-week suspended ban, with Southampton opting to stand by their manager amid the controversy. But despite the points deduction, Southampton sit five points off the top of the table after a stellar start to the season. Eckert said: "We've had some conversations that started a couple of weeks ago, and the goal was always clear: to show the same commitment that we have had for the last 12 months. I'm very happy that we have come to the point that we can make it official now. "There is a lot that has happened in the last 12 months, but the commitment from the club, from Dragan, Johannes and Phil, and the supporters, means everything to me. I am very grateful for that. item.title: OFFICIAL: Courtois signs Real Madrid contract extension
item.description: Real Madrid have announced the extension of Thibaut Courtois’ contract with the club until the summer of 2028. Per Realmadrid.com Real Madrid C.F. and Thibaut Courtois have agreed to extend our player’s contract, which ties him to the club until June 30, 2028. Thibaut Courtois joined Real Madrid in 2018. In his nine seasons wearing our jersey, he has played 348 matches and won 14 titles: 2 Champions League titles, 3 Club World Cups, 2 UEFA Super Cups, 3 La Liga titles, 1 Copa del Rey, and 3 Spanish Super Cups. His contribution to all these titles has been marked by decisive performances that have established him as the best goalkeeper in the world. He is an international with Belgium, having played 115 matches for his national team so far. Individually, Thibaut Courtois has won the Golden Glove at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, The Best FIFA Goalkeeper Award in 2018, the Yashin Trophy in 2022, and the Zamora Trophy in 2014. Additionally, he was included twice in the FIFA FIFPro World XI in 2022 and 2023 and was named the Best Player of the Champions League Final in Paris 2022, Real Madrid’s Fourteenth European Cup victory. Courtois is 34 years old but is arguably the world’s best goalkeeper, so this one-year extension makes sense.

item.title: Liverpool boss Taylor impressed with goalscoring form of forward Olsson
item.description: Liverpool boss Taylor impressed with goalscoring form of forward Olsson Liverpool head coach Gareth Taylor says that forward Beata Olsson’s recent goalscoring form has been impressive. The Swedish international has netted six goals in the last four games. She has helped Liverpool win three of those matches. Speaking to the media ahead of this weekend’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture against Chelsea, Liverpool head coach Taylor said that Olsson’s run of form has been impressive whilst highlighting areas where she can improve further. “Beata will always tell you that there’s way more to come from her,” Taylor said. “She’s definitely a very hungry player, great to work with. She is very honest in her appraisal of herself in games and in training. Like most strikers, she is desperate to score in every game and is super-frustrated when she doesn’t. Of course, she contributes more than that for us as a player, but you know that Beata has these spells where she really catches fire. “For her, it will always be about how many chances she gets in a game, how many times she makes the goalkeeper work. The more she does that, the more chances she has of scoring. She is a good finisher, there is no doubt about that, but I think getting her in the right positions, getting players to connect with her more is really important for us as a team. “She’s been good. Six goals in four games is really impressive.” Latest opponents Chelsea arrive on Merseyside top of the Barclays Women’s Super League table, but Taylor believes that his side will go into the game with confidence. He said “It’s a good game. We’ve both had quick turnarounds with us playing Wednesday night and it’s an early kick-off as well. “Good for us to be at St Helens. We had success in this fixture last year by taking a draw, but both teams will look slightly different to what they did then. “We feel pretty confident that we can attack this game like we would any other game. Our performances against the top teams have been good and positive this season. Looking forward to the challenge.” Liverpool have won their last three games, scoring 11 goals in the process. Taylor says that The Reds had been impressive even before those positive results. He said “Small wins for us, of course; two wins in the cup and a good win away at Brighton. “We are good in confidence. I’ve spoken to the players a lot; even though our results before that were a little bit tricky, I was impressed with our performances and knew that we weren’t far away from what we have achieved in the last three games. We’ve managed to score 11 goals against decent opposition in those three games. “We know the challenge tomorrow is really tough. They have a good level of players and they’re a good team, so we need to be at our very best to have a chance of taking points from the game.” Liverpool’s Barclays Women’s Super League fixture against Chelsea takes place at BrewDog Stadium in St Helens at 12.45pm on Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Bubba Wallace’s Team Makes Another Risky Decision
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images 23XI Racing is changing the leadership atop two of its teams for 2027, and Bubba Wallace will have a new voice directing his efforts from the pit box. The organization announced Nov. 18 that Davin Restivo will replace Charles Denike as crew chief of Wallace’s No. 23 Toyota. Denike will move to the No. 67 team to work with Corey Heim, who is preparing for his first full-time NASCAR Cup Series season. Tyler Reddick will retain Billy Scott as crew chief of the No. 45 team. The changes follow a productive season for 23XI. The organization recorded eight victories in 2026, including six by Reddick and two by Heim. Wallace did not reach Victory Lane, but he finished the year with 17 top-10 results, five top-five finishes and two runner-up performances. Wallace and Denike had previously enjoyed success together, including their victory in the 2025 Brickyard 400. Their partnership ends after two seasons, with 23XI choosing to take a different approach as it looks to build a championship contender. The team says the moves are about matching personnel strengths to each driver’s needs. Dave Rogers, 23XI’s senior director of competition, explained that Denike’s calm leadership style should benefit Heim as he makes the jump to a full-time Cup schedule. Rogers also pointed to Restivo’s relentless attitude and attention to detail as qualities that make him a good fit for Wallace. Denny Hamlin, 23XI’s co-owner, emphasized that the organization wants to build on its winning season rather than settle for its current results. “While this was a banner year for us in the win column, it has always been our goal to build a championship-caliber organization,” Hamlin said in the team’s announcement. For Wallace, the change brings another opportunity to turn consistent finishes into victories. Restivo spent the past two seasons leading Riley Herbst’s team at 23XI, so he already knows the organization and its expectations. The new pairing will have to prove itself on the track, but 23XI is making clear that its ambitions extend beyond simply adding to its win total. The goal is to put all three teams in a stronger position to compete for a Cup Series championship .

item.title: Confirmed: Real Madrid squad list to face Celta Vigo | La Liga MD 13
item.description: Confirmed: Real Madrid squad list to face Celta Vigo | La Liga MD 13 With the international break out of the way, Real Madrid are back in action on Sunday as they get set to lock horns with Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu on Matchday 13 of the 2026/27 La Liga. Having strung together an impressive run of eight wins prior to the break, Real Madrid will be eager to carry on from where they left off and secure all three points against Claudio Giraldez & co. tomorrow. Ahead of tomorrow’s match, Los Blancos manager Jose Mourinho has announced the squad list of players who will be at his disposal for selection. The biggest headline is that key superstar Vinicius Jr. is back in the squad for Real Madrid after having missed the last four games in La Liga due to a suspension for his red card against Villarreal. The 26-year-old attacker has missed the games against Sevilla, Barcelona, Racing Santander, and Valencia. Having scored five goals in two games for Brazil during the international break, he will hope to carry on in the same vein of form for his club. Aurelien Tchouameni and Bernardo Silva, who returned with minor injuries during the break, have been declared fit and are in the squad to face Celta Vigo. Meanwhile, Raul Asencio and Rodrygo remain unavailable as they continue to recover from their fitness issues. Ferland Mendy was expected to be recalled to the squad, having been training with the group for some time now, but Mourinho has opted not to include the veteran left-back.

item.title: Foxes announce new sponsor after porn actress row
item.description: BC Game has been the main shirt sponsor of Leicester City for two and a half years [Getty Images] Leicester City have announced a new main shirt sponsor after ending a partnership with a gambling firm following its appointment of a porn actress as its brand ambassador. The League One side confirmed they have now partnered with Bossjob, an AI-powered recruitment and job-matching platform based in Singapore. On Wednesday, the club announced its split with BC Game - which was named as a sponsor for the Foxes at the start of the 2024-25 season. The club's commercial director, Russell Jones, said the new men's team sponsor would be in place for the remainder of the 2026-27 season. The Foxes parted ways with BC Game, an online gambling company not available to UK users, after it named porn actress Eva Elfie as a brand ambassador earlier this month. Announcing the partnership , the firm posted a video of Elfie and a delivery driver on social media, with the caption: "Welcome to BC Game Eva Elfie! Let the fun begin." In response, fan group The Foxes Trust said: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people. "Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?" On Wednesday, following the criticism, the club issued a statement, which said it and BC Game had "reached a mutual agreement to conclude our commercial partnership with immediate effect". In a further statement on Friday, the Foxes confirmed Bossjob will take up the front-of-shirt position from this Saturday at their League One match against Huddersfield Town. Jones said: "We welcome Bossjob as our new principal partner for the remainder of the season and look forward to building a strong relationship over the coming months. "Through the partnership, we look forward to introducing Bossjob to our supporters and wider audiences, while supporting the company's ambitions to develop its international profile." The club said replica shirts featuring the new sponsor would be made available to fans "in the coming days". Bossjob co-founder, Quak Kiat How, added: "We're pleased to begin this partnership with Leicester City, a football club with a proud history and a strong connection to its supporters and local community. "We look forward to working with Leicester City throughout the remainder of the season." Listen to BBC Radio Leicester on Sounds and follow BBC Leicester on Facebook , on X , or on Instagram . item.title: Andriy Shevchenko slams Mykhailo Mudryk for ‘baseless slander’ after Ukraine doping claim
item.description: Ukrainian football federation president Andriy Shevchenko has issued a sharp rebuke to Mykhailo Mudryk after the Chelsea winger blamed the national team for his positive drugs test. Mudryk tested positive for the banned substance meldonium in 2024 , and was initially banned for four years by the Football Association . He successfully appealed against the length of his ban to the Court of Arbitration for Sport , and returned to football in July 2026. Speaking in an interview with Ukrainian YouTube channel Guest of Gordon, Mudryk, who is on a season-long loan at Tottenham, laid the blame on “the environment in the Ukrainian national team” for his suspension. He said: “I had never heard of a drug like meldonium . It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England.” He said he had only been in Ukraine with the national team, which “points to the fact it was in a national team camp”. Former Chelsea and AC Milan forward Shevchenko, now president of the Ukrainian Association of Football (UAF), called such claims “baseless slander” and said that “numerous investigations and audits” had been unable to identify how or when the meldonium entered Mudryk’s system. He alleged that Mudryk’s camp had tried to convince a staff member at the UAF to take the blame for the 25-year-old’s positive test. Shevchenko said: “His representatives repeatedly approached the UAF with a proposal to find an employee who would falsely take responsibility for the meldonium found in his doping sample. “The UAF refused, as such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work.” Shevchenko criticised his compatriot for “baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally”, and challenged Mudryk to provide evidence for his claims, including that he had received little support from the federation during the doping case. He added: “I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. “If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologise to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.”

item.description: Football icon Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink has said that he wants his former club Middlesbrough to finally end a decade of exile from the Premier League this season. Boro narrowly missed out on automatic promotion last campaign after being consistently in the race before losing to a late Oli McBurnie goal in the play-off final. Kim Hellberg’s side currently sit second in the Championship table, level on points with leaders Birmingham. Hasselbaink said “They’ve been flirting with promotion during the last three or four years. The problem that Boro have had is being able to sustain what they’ve built in the second half of the season. “I would love to see them get back up there, because Boro are a special club in a really special part of the world. “Football means everything to the people in that town, and they deserve a club in the Premier League. “Hopefully they can sustain that momentum. Let’s be honest though, as much as I would love to see them do it, it will be really, really difficult. “The Championship is such a difficult league to get out of – Boro has been trying for almost a decade. item.title: How ex-West Ham striker Dylan Tombides has left a legacy
item.description: It is 15 years since former West Ham United striker Dylan Tombides was diagnosed with cancer following his participation at the Fifa Under-17 World Cup, but his legacy is now helping educate the next generation at the latest edition of the tournament in Qatar. After the former Australia youth international died from the disease in 2014, Dylan's mother, Tracey Lee, and brother, Taylor Tombides, launched the DT38 Foundation. Now working in partnership with Fifa, they are raising awareness of testicular cancer, the most common cancer among males aged 15 to 44, through Dylan's story. He made one first-team appearance for West Ham before his death aged 20. "To be linked with Fifa is the top of the mountain, as far as we're concerned," Lee said. "It puts legitimacy to what we are doing and, as far as does it help us with the grief? Yes, it helps us because we know we're saving lives. "We've got messages from people saying: 'I thought of Dylan's story when I found a lump and I knew not to delay. I had testicular cancer and now I'm cancer-free and Dylan saved my life'. "That tells us that what we're doing is life-changing for that family, that person." Dylan Tombides displayed a happy birthday message to his mum after scoring in the 2011 Fifa Under-17 World Cup [Getty Images] Each participating team has received a presentation on recognising the signs of testicular cancer and the importance of self-examination. Some sessions initially prompted laughter and jokes among players when testicles were discussed in front of team-mates. However, Fifa medical director, Dr Andrew Massey, said the message had resonated across all 48 teams, featuring 1,200 players, as Lee shared the story of her son's diagnosis and treatment. "Dylan went to his GP," she said. "He decided he didn't want to go to the club doctors because they were in a relegation battle and he wanted them to focus on football in 2011. "So he went to the GP and he said, 'Don't worry, mate, it's just a cyst and people live with cysts all the time.' "So Dylan finished the season with West Ham, flew out to Australia to join his team-mates there and trained out there until they went to Mexico. "And it was out at Mexico that they pulled Dylan for a random drug test and it came back positive for a banned substance or a tumour. "And as it turned out, Dylan then finally got correctly diagnosed with testicular cancer, and then started with the removal of his testicle and three years of really intense chemotherapy." She added: "I remember sitting there having a conversation with Dylan and they were saying the next treatment has a 10% chance of working. And we know how that turned out. "It's that story that prompted young players from the Jamaican youth national team to say 'I am so sorry for your loss' with conversations with the French team ending in hugs and handshakes."

item.title: Nick Wright says one NFL player is sneakily having an MVP level season
item.description: Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Nick Wright has floated the idea that Jaxon Smith-Njigba could be in contention for the 2026 NFL MVP award. The Seattle Seahawks as a team have declined this year, already losing four games after going 14-3 en route to the Super Bowl in the previous campaign. But while they have fallen off, Smith-Njigba is still one of the best receivers in the NFL in the current season. He has the most receiving yards (1,207) of any player by a considerable distance, with CeeDee Lamb (976) second. Jaxon is also leading the league in receiving touchdowns (10) and has the most receptions (79) ahead of the weekend’s action. In turn, it is perhaps not surprising that, when speaking via What’s Wright? With Nick Wright this week, Wright shared his opinion that Smith-Njigba could be a sneaky argument for MVP. He said: “The Lions can just hand the ball to Jahmyr Gibbs. That’s not how it works with JSN. And JSN has been doing it with two different quarterbacks, which I think is super impressive. I think JSN sneaky has an MVP argument, like Barnwell talked about. Everybody knows he’s the only way they can move the ball, and no one can slow him down.” History suggests Jaxon Smith-Njigba won’t be named MVP While the Seahawks wide receiver is no doubt in great form right now, the NFL has made a habit of only really giving the MVP award to quarterbacks. In fact, since 2012, running back Adrian Peterson is the only non-quarterback to pick up the prize: 2025 – Matthew Stafford (QB) 2024 – Josh Allen (QB) 2023 – Lamar Jackson (QB) 2022 – Patrick Mahomes (QB) 2021 – Aaron Rodgers (QB) 2020 – Aaron Rodgers (QB) 2019 – Lamar Jackson (QB) 2018 – Patrick Mahomes (QB) 2017 – Tom Brady (QB) 2016 – Matt Ryan (QB) 2015 – Cam Newton (QB) 2014 – Aaron Rodgers (QB) 2013 – Peyton Manning (QB) 2012 – Adrian Peterson (RB) Furthermore, a wide receiver has never actually been named the MVP during the history of the award. With that in mind, this year’s accolade will most likely end up in the hands of someone like Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy or Josh Allen. item.title: Jordan Reid Projects Dolphins To Skip Quarterback For Edge Rusher
item.description: Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images On Wednesday, Jordan Reid of ESPN published his initial 2027 mock draft, envisioning Texas edge rusher Colin Simmons being chosen by the Dolphins with the third overall pick. This choice comes despite the team holding a 1-8 record and likely owning that high slot. Reid argues Miami needs a defensive star more than another quarterback right now. The Dolphins have struggled to pressure opposing quarterbacks all season, recording just 13 sacks through nine games. That total stands as the fewest in the NFL. A Perfect Fit for Jeff Hafley The pairing of Simmons with existing talent creates a scary front for opposing offenses. Reid points out that the Dolphins already drafted Chop Robinson in the first round of 2024. Robinson has shown improvement after a tough 2025 season, but he needs help. “Pairing Simmons with 2024 first-rounder Chop Robinson would give the Dolphins an explosive pass-rush duo for defensive-minded coach Jeff Hafley.” This combination could finally give Miami’s defense a pass rusher that offenses have to fear.

Stetson started off hot, hitting 9 of their first 12 shots before Louisville woke up. Down 22-14, Flory Bidunga scored 7 straight points to rally the home team. Stetson held the lead until about the 5:31 mark, which is impressive. In the second half, Louisville cranked up the D, forcing Stetson to miss 18 of 20 attempts over about nine minutes. Incidentally, Karter Knox took Seth Trimble’s starting spot and finished with 14 points and 10 rebounds. Is it just us, or is it nice to see a bit of optimism for Notre Dame? Auburn battled back in the second, but the Tigers missed six straight free throws late in the second half, then Braeden Smith hit a tough shot in the lane to put Notre Dame up by 77-73. Brady Koehler, who is getting some NBA buzz, stole Auburn’s inbounds pass, and hit a free throw to put the game out of reach. NC State was hot against Murray State, hitting 16-0f-28 threes for 57.1 percent. Christian Bliss had 16, while Nick Townsend kicked in 11. Cal broke the game open early, and never really was challenged. The Bears forced an impressive 24 turnovers, which they converted into 28 points. Nojus Indrusaitis had 23 points, while Michael Cooper added 18. item.title: Deshaun Watson Wants to Return, Continue to 'Build on the Legacy'
item.description: theOBR BEREA,Ohio — Ever since Cleveland Browns owner Jimmy Haslam proclaimed the trade for quarterback Deshaun Watson was a ‘big swing and miss’ at the NFL owners meetings in March of 2025, Browns fans had—for the most part—turned the page on the Watson era with the Browns. Even when Todd Monken was named the Browns newest head coach in January and he declared an open competition between Watson and second-year quarterback Shedeur Sanders, most assumed Watson was just going to be phased out being in the final year of his unprecedented contract that paid him $230 million, fully guaranteed. At the time of the trade in March 2022, it was the biggest contract in NFL history and first, fully guaranteed contract. The Browns also gave up six draft choices in the trade, including three first round picks. Before the 2026 season started, Watson had missed 49 of 68 games with the Browns due to an 11-game suspension from the NFL in 2022 and injuries in 2023-2025, including a broken bone in his throwing shoulder and a twice-ruptured Achilles tendon that sidelined him for all of 2025. However, Watson was tabbed by Monken after training camp as the starting quarterback after not playing in nearly two seasons and despite a rough start has stuck with him through 10 games. Even when Watson missed the Saints game after not practicing the week leading up to the game due to a concussion, Monken named Watson the starter for the Texans game, despite Sanders throwing for 297 yards in an overtime loss. Watson rewarded him with a come-from-behind, game-winning drive to give the Browns a 27-24 win and a 6-4 record at the bye. Watson, 31, has completed 65.1 percent of his passes for 2,118 yards. He is 11th in the NFL in completions, 16th in yardage, seven touchdowns (tied for 26th), four interceptions (tied for fourth-fewest). His 7.3 yards per attempt is 13th in the NFL and his 89.1 QB rating is 18th in the NFL. Watson has rushed 59 times for 266 yards and two touchdowns. The nine games that Watson has started in 2026 is the most he has played since joining the Browns. Despite being inconsistent, Watson has led the Browns to a 6-4 record, including six game-winning drives in the fourth quarter. Watson’s game-winning drive in the final two minutes last week against the Texans was his sixth of the season. He joined Troy Aikman in 1990 and Matthew Stafford in 2016 as the only quarterbacks to lead winning drives in the fourth quarter in each of their team’s first six victories. Watson is now tied with Bernie Kosar, who had six game-winning drives in the fourth-quarter in 1986. He is behind only Brian Sipe, who had seven in 1979 for most in a season in franchise history. Image via @iam_chaycemcdInstagram The Chicago Cubs have claimed 28-year-old right-handed pitcher Chayce McDermott off waivers from the New York Mets in the 2026-27 MLB offseason. No corresponding roster move was required, since Chicago already had open spots on its 40-man roster after protecting prospects ahead of the Rule 5 Draft. McDermott spent the 2026 season with the Baltimore Orioles, Los Angeles Dodgers and Mets. He posted a 5.87 ERA in 7.2 innings in five appearances. In his MLB career, he holds a 1-1 record and a 10.18 ERA across 10 appearances, including two starts. Fans shared their thoughts on the latest acquisition by the Cubs. “Imagine claiming a pitcher who was waived by the Mets. LOL,” one fan wrote. Several more fans came up with sarcastic remarks: These reactions make it clear that Cubs fans are not happy with this acquisition. Chicago fans expect major moves this offseason from the front office after being eliminated in the 2026 wild-card round during the postseason. The Cubs may have acquired McDermott due to his strikeout potential in the minor leagues. In six seasons, he has posted a 25-27 record with a 4.31 ERA, 625 strikeouts, and 278 walks in 445 innings pitched. McDermott is out of minor-league options, according to CubsHQ . That means Chicago cannot freely send him between the majors and minors without exposing him to waivers. Cubs Take Interest In Japanese Triple Crown Winner The Cubs need a couple of outfielders this offseason after Seiya Suzuki, Ian Happ, Michael Conforto, and Tyrone Taylor became free agents this winter. Currently, they have Pete Crow-Armstrong, Matt Shaw, Pedro Ramirez, and Kevin Alcantara in the outfield room. The Cubs have reportedly taken an interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato to address their outfield depth, per Patrick Mooney of The Athletic . Sato was posted by the Hanshin Tigers on November 1. Therefore, he has until Dec. 16 to sign with an MLB team. The Japanese 6-foot-1 slugger hit .277/.345/.579 with 40 home runs, 34 doubles, four triples, 102 RBI, and 10 stolen bases in 139 games in 2025 to win the Central League MVP award. Last season, he won the NPB Central League Triple Crown after hitting .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs, 40 doubles, three triples, 106 RBI, and eight stolen bases in 143 games. item.title: Houston leaves no doubt who should be college basketball’s new No. 1
item.description: Guess what, everybody? Kelvin Sampson and his Houston Cougars are back. Men's college basketball is about to have a new No. 1 team, and there's no doubt Houston belongs at the top after beating No. 9 Kansas 92-83 to win the Players Era 8 tournament, capping one of the most impressive runs of the young season. As the premier early season event , there's plenty of value in navigating the loaded field in Las Vegas and emerging victorious. Just ask Michigan last season. Houston didn't just win. The Cougars were dang near perfect. After taking down No. 1 Florida in the semifinal , the Cougars faced a Big 12 foe in Kansas that could very well meet them again in the conference championship game, possibly even the Final Four. Against the Jayhawks, though, it didn't look like a big-time battle. It looked like a coming-out party for Houston. The Cougars came right out and did what they do best: make life extremely annoying for opponents with relentless defense. Then came what quite possibly separates this team from the rest of the country: the complementary offense. Bill Self couldn't burn through his timeouts fast enough as Houston made life look way too easy around the basket, putting the Jayhawks in a blender for easy buckets Kansas couldn't seem to stop. It was a dominant first half. Houston led by as many as 24 points and entered halftime with 54, the most it has scored against a top-25 team in the past 30 years. Even when Kansas staged a furious comeback behind freshman star Tyran Stokes, cutting the deficit to four points with just under three minutes remaining, Houston didn't flinch. The Cougars scored the next eight points to put the dagger in. It took three tries, but Houston has finally emerged from Players Era as a champion after unsuccessful attempts in 2024 and 2025. New No. 1 team is clear There will be massive reshuffling in the USA TODAY Sports Coaches Poll after the top four teams all lost , and you don't have to look far to see who should be the new No. 1 on Monday, Nov. 23: the Cougars themselves. Not only did Houston win the Players Era 8, but it also had the toughest path of any team in the field as the only one to play two top-10 opponents. It beat both of them convincingly. The Cougars bullied the Gators in the rematch of the 2025 national championship game , unfazed by the pristine frontcourt of Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon and Rueben Chinyelu. Houston outmuscled Florida inside while guard Dedan Thomas Jr. lit up the Gators. If anything, the Cougars' toughest challenge came against Rutgers in the opening round, a game they still won by 12 points. item.title: The Colts should “evaluate” Shane Steichen
item.description: HOUSTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 19: Head coach Shane Steichen of the Indianapolis Colts looks on against the Houston Texans during the fourth quarter of the game at Reliant Stadium on November 19, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images “We’ll evaluate everything.” Have you heard that before? It’s becoming a canned phrase and mantra for Indianapolis Colts head coach Shane Steichen. The most recent example comes after the Colts were ripped apart by the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football. That’s a smart move, Shane. Maybe the Colts organization needs to do the same for you too. The Colts sit at 3-8 on the year, and Steichen’s overall record is 28-34. The man who was brought in due to his success with Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia offense was unable to mold Anthony Richardson in the same fashion or create results. Zero postseason appearances and a 7-25 record when the opponent is over .500 make the case why he needs to be heavily scrutinized. It is wise to consider benching Daniel Jones. Does it get better? Maybe not. That’s on Chris Ballard and Steichen, however. Steichen had a choice between the two men at quarterback. Not that his options were necessarily glowing, but he picked Jones to be his guy. From the onset, it looked like a stroke of genius. Now, it looks disastrous. He can evaluate all he wants. The Colts organization should do the same. It isn’t just Steichen, but it starts there. Based on the last four years of data, the case can be made that a change in leadership is needed. Evaluating is normally a good thing. What can trip one up is the timing. Shane Steichen’s “evaluation” of Daniel Jones and the quarterback position might be too little, too late to save his job. Steichen’s time with the franchise might be drawing to a close, but the Colts organization will live on. Their time for evaluation is now. It starts with the head coach.

item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 23: MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred speaks with the media prior to game one of the 2026 World Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field on October 23, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images When we’re in school, we hear a lot about propaganda. American history textbooks show us political cartoons from the late 19th and early 20th century about the abolition of slavery, the rise of industrial robber-barons, and the progressive movement. European art historians discuss how Louis XIV used paintings and sculptures to present himself as the “Sun King” as he strengthened the power of the French crown over the First and Second Estates. In my own Roman history classes, I spend multiple weeks demonstrating how the emperors employed literature, history, sculpture, and construction projects to assert the supremacy of both Rome and the imperial household. Whether in middle school, high school, or college, students regularly grapple with propaganda in their history classes, learning how people with access to communicative resources have been able to present their own version of reality to sway public opinion in their favor. Once we’re out of school, though, propaganda falls by the wayside, and ceases to be a concern. It exists, in the public consciousness at least, not as a part of our lives, but as a historical oddity, the behavior of a bygone era — or, when it’s acknowledged in the modern world, as something that happens in the nebulous “over there,” not “here.” And yet, what else can we call the flood of political advertisements in every commercial break that made the World Series borderline unwatchable if not propaganda? After all, are they not trying to sell their version of reality, as opposed to that of their opponents, in an effort to sway voters? Propaganda is most often understood in terms of politics, but it doesn’t have to be. And right now, we’re living in what I call a sports propaganda moment, as two major entities — the NCAA and Major League Baseball — have gone on the figurative warpath, spending millions of dollars in advertising not to get people to watch their product, but to generate outrage from fans on their own behalf against that of their players. item.description: Photo by Rich Storry/TGL/TGL Golf via Getty Images Tiger Woods will return to action in just two weeks’ time at the Hero World Challenge in the Bahamas. Woods has not played a competitive tournament since The Open Championship in July 2024, and he has experienced all sorts of problems away from the golf course since then. The 15-time major champion has been involved in two serious car accidents and has been in and out of rehab in order to get a handle on his addiction to painkillers. However, Tiger Woods is nothing if he is not a fighter, and there is no way that he will bow out of the game without making one final push to try and win what would be a record-setting 83rd PGA Tour title. Woods is expected to play some big events in 2027, including The Genesis Invitational, The Masters and The Open Championship. However, he may well be looking to play certain PGA Tour Champions events as well, in order to beef out his schedule and to get some competitive reps under his belt ahead of the majors. Stewart Cink on Tiger Woods potentially competing on PGA Tour Champions Cink has spoken to SiriusXM PGA TOUR Radio about Tiger Woods potentially playing on PGA Tour Champions in 2027. The 2009 Open champion responded when asked whether Woods would actually be welcome on the senior tour. “ We would love for Tiger to come play, and he’s one of the guys I have in mind when I constantly say, like, guys are gonna like it out there, “ Cink explained. “ I just think Tiger is a golfer at heart. He wants to compete, but I don’t know any of his plans. I hope he does. It would be great for the tour and I think it would be good for him too. “ He would really love it, to see some new venues and it’s just, it’s competitive golf. He’s going to get in contention and have a chance to win a whole lot of tournaments. Not that that’s anything new to him, but he still thrives on it. I think it’s something that never gets old for anybody. “ So I wish him the best. It’s going to be great to see him back playing. “ It would be great to see Tiger Woods play on PGA Tour Champions in 2027. He would surely love to compete against many of his old rivals, including the likes of Ernie Els, Vijay Singh, Retief Goosen and Padraig Harrington. It would also be slightly easier on his body, with 54-hole tournaments and the use of golf carts available as well. Woods needs to ease back into action over the next few months, and playing one or two PGA Tour Champions events will be the best way for him to do just that.

item.title: Pep Guardiola Reunites With Fan-Favourite Manchester City Alumnus in Brazil
item.description: Pep Guardiola Reunites With Fan-Favourite Manchester City Alumnus in Brazil Some months on from his emotional departure from the Etihad Stadium earlier this year, Pep Guardiola has been making the most of a rare spell away from the dugout. He has not been short of suitors, mind, having recently been linked with the vacant United States job, though he is expected to reject the approach and prolong his break from management. In the meantime, he has been putting the downtime to good use, and one snapshot from his travels is sure to bring a smile to the faces of supporters back in Manchester. Guardiola has been pictured reuniting with an old friend from his trophy-laden years at the club, a familiar face who still holds fan-favourite status in the blue half of the city. A warm reunion in Brazil The man in question is Fernandinho, the much-loved former Manchester City midfielder, who shared a photograph of the pair together. Posting on Instagram , the Brazilian, smartly dressed and all smiles in an office, captioned the image simply: “So happy to have you here in Brazil, Pep.” Guardiola is in Brazil to watch City Football Group side Bahia , making the trip alongside Manchester City chief executive Ferran Soriano. The journey is part of the ambassadorial and technical advisory role Pep took up within City Football Group after bringing the curtain down on his spell in Manchester. Seeing the two together will stir fond memories for City supporters; Fernandinho was one of the few players Guardiola inherited in 2016 whom he trusted from the very outset. While the new manager set about reshaping the squad, the Brazilian quickly made himself indispensable, and he would remain a key figure for more than half a decade. Signed from Shakhtar Donetsk in 2013 at the age of 28, Fernandinho became the defensive anchor around which Guardiola built his finest sides. He was the shield in front of the back four during the record-breaking 2017/18 campaign, when City amassed 100 points with Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva pulling the strings ahead of him. He was arguably even better the following season, a pillar of the side that edged out Liverpool to the title by a single point, and earned a place in the PFA Team of the Year. When David Silva departed in 2020, it was Fernandinho who inherited the captain’s armband, leading the club with the same authority he had long shown on the pitch. By the time he left the Etihad in 2022 to return home with Athletico Paranaense, Fernandinho had collected five Premier League titles and cemented his standing as one of the most dependable servants of the Guardiola era. Now retired from playing, his bond with his former manager clearly endures, and it would be wise not to bet against the pair working together again some day down the line.
